basics.name: Stephen L. Lange
basics.label: Security Architect
basics.summary: Security professional with extensive architecture, engineering, administration and management experience. A leader at designing and delivering targeted IT solutions capable of meeting business needs while staying within budgetary & time constraints. A skilled problem solver and decision maker, team player and self-starter with a passion for technology.

work.name: CME GROUP
work.summary:
As a CME Group Infrastructure Security Architect, I provide leadership on security subject matter through design & delivery of integrated solution architectures and development of standards and reference architectures. As a Security Architect, I participate in all functions related to Infrastructure Security Architecture, including infrastructure security strategy and roadmap planning, acting as a security liaison to the business, and helping to facilitate demand management.

In my role as a Security Architect, I provide a high level of technical expertise in multiple disciplines within Infrastructure and Information Security, including networking, virtualization, identity and access management, directory services, cloud computing, databases, a basic understanding of security and regulatory frameworks (CIS, NIST, RegSCI, HIPAA, etc.), security stack technologies (IDS/IPS, SIEM, etc.) among other disciplines.

In addition, I provide security mentorship, offer security design guidance and consultation services to drive change and support the evolution of security at CME Group. As a Global Information Security team (GIS) leader, I engage with and support other leaders across GIS and Technology to ensure the timely delivery of security and business solutions. Daily responsibilities include:
highlights: Actively lead the creation and updating of standards and reference architectures to meet CME regulatory requirements (standards) and provide direction and guidance on proper compliance with these defined standards (reference architectures
Performing infrastructure assessments and making design change recommendations that provide risk remediation and proper design, structure, and implementation recommendations
Assist in planning the remediation of assessment, audit, and regulatory findings

Assisting with demand forecasting for Infrastructure Architecture services by meeting with CME business units to better understand their needs. Aid in the determination of necessary resource levels to support those business units’ needs.

Communicate and collaborate with cross-functional peers outside of the Technology Division, including General Counsel, Records Retention, Global Assurance, Enterprise Risk Management, Third-Party Risk Management, and other business unit leadership
Drive objectivity and build consensus among internal and external stakeholders with widely divergent perspectives and drivers
Interact with industry peers from other systemically important financial market utility (SIFMU) organizations, research organizations, solution providers, etc.

Participate in and contribute to key working groups across the enterprise, including but not limited to: Architecture Review Board and/or change advisory boards. Prepare reports for senior management including presentations, metrics, and other documentation required to support governance functions.

Assist with the continuous improvement and maturation of the methods, instrumentation, training, documentation, and processes required to properly assess and govern Infrastructure architecture and the software development lifecycle
Participate in the development of the security roadmap, and communicate security vision to business partners and IT staff
Actively participates in Communities of Practice to ensure effective adoption of security and continuous improvement of security efforts
Act as an advocate for security and lead efforts to promote security awareness at all levels of the organizations
Ensure that all risk considerations are identified and addressed with new and modified services
Monitor and enhance secure architecture standards within the Software Development Lifecycle
Identify and establish core architectural mechanisms to enhance the security of services
Support larger architectural projects while leading internal projects

work.name: TRANSUNION
work.summary: As a Senior Security Architect at TransUnion I worked to secure enterprise information by determining security requirements; planning, implementing, and testing security systems; preparing security standards, policies, and procedures; mentoring team members.
highlights: Performed security assessments for business units seeking to implement updated or new solutions, presented recommendations and findings to the enterprise architectural review board for consideration
Researched and wrote security standards and reference architectures
Developed governance scripts that were used to validate security standard controls and provide compliance metrics
Prepared system security reports by collecting, analyzing, and summarizing data and trends
Provided mentoring and skills transfer to new/developing security team members
Principal architect & SME for Tripwire Enterprise, Qualys, Symantec Encryption Server (PGP)
Assisted with PCI auditing compliance of systems using Tripwire Enterprise

work.name: UNITE HERE HEALTH
work.summary: Part auditor, investigator, and advisor, this position is tasked with identifying and abating potential threats to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of systems and data critical for continued operation & HIPAA privacy/security compliance.
highlights: Responsible for internal and external vulnerability & penetration testing using commercial and open-source software (Core Impact, Nessus)
Implemented Intrusion Detection System and unified AIX/Linux/Windows event log collection system
Performed security audits of deployed systems to identify potential regulatory compliance issues
Reviewed all Firewall and VPN changes and performed quarterly audits of firewall rules

work.name: UNITE HERE HEALTH
work.summary: Management of an eight-person team of network administrators and help desk personnel whose responsibilities included Windows, AIX, and Linux systems. A hands-on supervisor proficient in both supervisory and technical roles.
highlights: Responsible for the management and planning of nine data centers
Performed business needs assessment and annual IT budget forecasting

Successful design and implementation of multi-year technology acquisition plan that included upgrades to existing LAN/WAN infrastructure, storage, and server systems that resulted in a 33% reduction in maintenance costs and a 40% reduction in power costs
